page: Microsoft Azure E48ads_v7 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor hosted on Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance provides 48 dedicated vCPUs across 24 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, capable of clock speeds up to 4.5 GHz. The CPU architecture incorporates 48 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache, backed by vector and cryptographic extensions including AVX-512, AVX-VNNI, and AES-NI.

The instance delivers 384.0 GB of system memory, establishing an allocation ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Alongside external storage options, Azure bundles 2,835 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage for low-latency scratch space and temporary file operations. The hardware profile does not include GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, aligning its operational capacity with memory-bound and compute-heavy central processing workflows.

Benchmark measurements place the instance in the top tier for single-core stress-ng processing and multi-core Geekbench results, supported by strong uncached memory write throughput exceeding 100 GB/s. Database processing metrics show high performance with 78.13 million Redis SET operations per second and strong PassMark database operations scores. These characteristics make the E48ads_v7 suitable for enterprise relational database engines, large Redis or Memcached clusters, in-memory data processing, and large software build environments requiring dense RAM and fast local disk access.
